Article Title: Wall Street's AI jitters return as stocks tumble, S&P500 logs longest losing streak in 2.5 years
Article Text:
Wall Street takes another hit

Anthropic's strong debut fails to lift mood

AI stocks give up early gains as selling returns

AI bubble: Why investors are worried

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Asian markets mixed, European stocks end lower

Wall Street took another hit on Thursday as the AI party appeared to be losing its fizz. US stocks tumbled again as investors continued to dump AI-linked shares, questioning whether the technology's spectacular rally had finally run out of steam.Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut, which saw its shares soar well above the expected price, failed to lift the mood, as worries over sky-high valuations, expensive borrowing and whether massive AI investments will pay off kept investors on edge.The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The index is now 8.2% below the record high it touched last month.The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points, or 2.3%. The sell-off was broad-based, with more than 90% of the stocks in the S&P500 ending the day lower.The market initially showed signs of recovery after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, made its stock market debut on Thursday.The company priced its shares at $83 each, higher than its earlier expected range of $70 to $78.Soon after trading began on the Nasdaq shortly before noon, the shares climbed above $115.The strong debut briefly lifted the S&P500 by as much as 1.3%. However, the gains did not last. Anthropic shares eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from their IPO price.The strong demand for the shares showed that investors were still interested in AI companies, despite the recent fall in their stock prices. However, the positive response to Anthropic's listing was not enough to stop the wider market decline.Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, described the current market conditions as “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”Several major AI-linked stocks started Thursday's session with gains but later slipped into losses.Micron Technology, which has benefited from rising demand for computer memory because of the AI boom, initially gained 7.8%. However, it reversed course and ended the day 2.1% lower.CoreWeave, which buys AI chips and rents access to them to customers through the cloud, also saw its shares swing sharply. After rising 10.5% in the morning, the stock ended the session down 6.1%.Nvidia shares followed a similar pattern. The stock erased its early gain of 4.7% and closed 3.3% lower as concerns about the AI industry continued to weigh on investors.The recent fall in AI stocks comes amid growing concerns about whether their high prices can be justified.One of the biggest worries is that shares of AI companies may have become too expensive after their sharp rise. Investors are also questioning whether AI will generate enough profits and improve productivity enough to justify the huge amounts companies are spending on data centres.High interest rates have added to these concerns. With borrowing becoming more expensive, investors fear that companies may find it harder to raise the money needed to expand their AI businesses.Political developments have also added to the uncertainty. Sweeping victories for Democrats in the US midterm elections this month have raised concerns that AI companies could face more regulations.Another development adding to the concerns was the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was one of the biggest supporters of the AI industry and helped build investor interest in the technology. He also used some of Nvidia's huge profits to support the industry's growth.In the bond market, US treasury yields declined as investors moved towards investments considered safer amid the fall in stock prices.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury slipped to 5.04% from 5.07% on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, so when bond prices rise, their yields fall.Elsewhere, stock markets remained mixed.Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%, helped by a 4.6% gain in SoftBank Group. The company was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and a competitor to Anthropic.South Korea's Kospi also gained 1.4%, supported by a rise in stocks linked to the AI boom.However, stocks were weaker in other parts of Asia and Europe. Germany's DAX fell 1.1%.At the end of Thursday's trading session, the S&P 500 dropped 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points to close at 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points to 23,879.20.
Article Summary: The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%. Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut failed to lift the mood.

Article Title: Stock market holiday today: Are BSE, NSE closed on November 24 for Guru Nanak Jayanti?
Article Text:
This is the second-last stock market holiday of 2026.

Why are NSE and BSE closed today?

When will stock market trading resume?

Global markets rebound after Wall Street rally

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The BSE and NSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 24, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev or Guru Nanak Jayanti . Commodity trading on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), however, will resume during the evening session.This is the second-last stock market holiday of 2026, with the final one scheduled for December 25 on account of Christmas.The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) have declared November 24 a trading holiday for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev, also known as Guru Nanak Jayanti.Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives, securities lending and borrowing (SLB), capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market segments.The MCX will follow a partial trading schedule, with its morning session closed from 9 am to 5 pm. Trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11.30 pm.The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) will remain closed for the entire day.The holiday comes after a sharp sell-off in domestic equities on Monday, with both benchmark indices declining nearly 1.8% amid heavy selling in banking and metal stocks, weakness in global markets and profit booking following the recent rally.The Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65, down 450.95 points or 1.75%, while the BSE Sensex settled at 82,435.99, declining 1,483.72 points or 1.77%.Selling pressure was broad-based, with banking and commodity stocks bearing the brunt of the decline. The Nifty Bank index fell more than 3% to 62,585 after recently touching an all-time high, while the Nifty Metal index recorded the steepest sectoral decline, shedding 3.70%.The Nifty IT index was the only major sectoral index to close in positive territory, gaining 1.8%.Trading on the NSE and BSE will resume on Wednesday, November 25, with regular market hours. The MCX will also operate its regular morning and evening sessions on Wednesday, while the NCDEX will resume trading after the holiday.The next and final scheduled stock market holiday of the year will be December 25 for Christmas, apart from regular weekend closures.Asian shares surged on Tuesday following a strong rally on Wall Street, as technology and AI-related stocks rebounded sharply after recent losses.MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6%, recovering from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks.Japan's Nikkei rose 4.5% as traders returned after a local holiday, while South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5% and Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1%.Nvidia shares rallied 31.5% on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in market value. The rally also lifted other AI-related stocks, with the Nasdaq 100 jumping more than 6%.The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite surged 4.7% and 6.5%, respectively, while S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2% early on Tuesday.Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling 3.5% lower at $89.37 on Monday. Gold also recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot prices rising 0.7% to $3,657.97 an ounce as investors bought the dip.
Article Summary: The BSE and NSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 24, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev. Commodity trading, however, will resume during the evening session. This is the second-last stock market holiday of 2026, with the final one scheduled for December 25.

Article Title: Gold price crash: From Rs 1.80 lakh to below Rs 1.25 lakh, will gold now plunge to Rs 1 lakh per 10 gms?
Article Text:

Why has gold been crashing in 2026?

So, is there an end in sight to this fall? What should investors do, and does the crash mean that gold has lost its safe haven appeal. We ask experts:

Will gold fall to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams?

What Jateen Trivedi said

Has gold lost its safe haven status?

What Manav Modi said

What should investors do and what’s the outlook for 2027?

What Maneesh Sharma said

Gold is no longer glittery or shining - in fact gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In 2025, there seemed no end in sight for gold’s spectacular rally. Come 2026, the year started with the yellow metal hitting a lifetime high of Rs 1.8 lakh per 10 grams in futures contract.And then the story went downhill - with no immediate bottom in sight!In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce, its lowest level in over a year. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. The crash has been relatively less in India because the government hiked customs duty on gold and silver earlier this year, cushioning the fall to some extent.Gold started falling in January as investors booked profit, but before it could find its equilibrium, the US-Iran war triggered another crash.Analysts say that the recent decline reflects a combination of profit-booking, liquidation of leveraged positions, changing interest-rate expectations and a stronger dollar.Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks, where investors sold liquid gold positions to raise cash or meet margin calls rather than using it as a shield while elevated bond yields and expectations of tighter interest rates in the US raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached. So, does that mean that there is a chance of gold prices falling to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams as well?Experts don’t rule out the possibility, though they believe that underlying fundamentals of gold such as central bank buying will continue to support the yellow metal. This indicates that a further fall may not sustain for long, they say.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says, “A decline towards Rs 1,00,000 cannot be ruled out if the rupee appreciates significantly and COMEX Gold corrects towards $3,000.”“However, the more important question is whether such lower levels can sustain and establish a long-term base. Given rapidly changing global investment themes and persistent geopolitical uncertainty, I do not expect prices to sustain below Rs 1,15,000 for long,” Trivedi tells TOI.Manav Modi, Commodities Analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd says, “The breach of Rs 1.25 lakh highlights how quickly sentiment and price expectations can change in a highly volatile market.”But, the analyst notes that a fall towards Rs 1 lakh would require a deeper strength in story as well positioning, potentially driven by sustained dollar strength, higher real yields, continued speculative unwinding and a moderation in investment demand.“However, the extent of the recent correction also needs to be assessed against gold’s underlying physical and central bank demand, which remains an important structural support,” he tells TOI.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma says that technically, the spot gold pair has extended a bearish phase following the recent breakdown below the previous consolidation phase.Moreover, the yellow metal holds well below the technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) validating the negative outlook.“While oversold technical indicators like RSI indicate that downside pace could slow but not yet reverse the trend. Having said that, a near term consolidation is still possible but could not stop the extension of a recent well established downtrend making gold vulnerable to fall further up to $3420-3380 / Oz in Spot (CMP $ 3575/Oz). On MCX futures, a sustainable close below Rs. 1,21,000/10 gm could accelerate its downtrend towards Rs. 1,18,000-1,16,000/10 gm on MCX,” he tells TOI.No.Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities believes that even though gold has witnessed a sharp correction, this does not mean it has lost its safe-haven status.“If we look at the two-year performance, prices have risen from around Rs 75,000 in January 2025 to nearly Rs 1,25,000 currently, delivering returns of approximately 55%,” Trivedi points out.“An asset that has preserved value for over 5,000 years will inevitably experience cycles of profit booking and corrections. Gold's safe-haven appeal remains intact; recent weakness reflects changing market dynamics rather than a loss of its investment relevance,” he adds.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma is of the view that gold’s long term role as a monetary and currency hedge still remains intact as long-term drivers like central bank buying and sovereign debt concerns remain relevant over time.But, Manav Modi cautions that while gold may not have lost its appeal as a safe haven asset, the recent price movements highlight that it is not immune to sharp corrections, particularly when speculative positioning becomes stretched.“Safe haven demand can also take a backseat when investors prioritise liquidity and reduce exposure across asset classes. Gold’s underlying role as a portfolio diversifier and reserve asset remains intact,” he tells TOI.Gold continues to be supported by central bank buying and recently ETF inflows. According to the latest World Gold Council report, Central bank buying jumped to 321t in Q3, eclipsing recent typical quarterly buying levels and lifting ytd demand to 675t. Gold ETFs reversed course following the Q2 outflows, adding 211t in Q3.So if the yellow metal continues to be a safe haven asset, what should your investment strategy in the current situation be?Experts believe the ongoing correction can be a good opportunity to accumulate gold, though cautiously and keeping your overall portfolio balance in mind.“This correction offers an opportunity to review gold allocation rather than panic over falling prices or focus on previous highs near Rs 1,80,000,” Jateen Trivedi says.“Investors should evaluate their overall portfolio allocation and consider staggered accumulation. Those with less than 15% allocation to gold may consider adding gradually, including a small lump-sum investment if significantly underinvested. The focus should be on long-term portfolio diversification rather than timing the exact bottom,” he recommends.Manav Modi recommends a staggered strategy to accumulate gold. “But, since further downside cannot be ignored, post some clarity, accumulation could be looked at,” he says.Finally, where is gold headed in 2027?Maneesh Sharma shares that a 20-25% recovery to around $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support which translates to a level of Rs 1,45,000-1,50,000/10 gm on MCX futures contract.Jateen Trivedi too believes that gold could move towards Rs 1,55,000-Rs 1,65,000 over the next year, depending on international prices and the rupee's trajectory.“COMEX Gold could potentially revisit the $4,500 zone, supported by central-bank demand and geopolitical uncertainty. However, continued rupee appreciation could limit domestic gains, resulting in Indian gold underperforming international prices,” he says.
Article Summary: Gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks.

Article Text:

Shares of Nvidia soared in trade on Monday after the tech giant announced the return of Jensen Huang as the company’s chief executive officer (CEO) with immediate effect. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave.The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. Earlier, the announcement triggered a sharp rally in the company's stock, which climbed more than 30% in premarket trading. The stock had recorded its steepest weekly fall since 2008 last week, after Huang’s removal from the CEO position unsettled investors and heightened worries about the future prospects of the AI sector.Jensen Huang’s unexpected return to the helm of Nvidia also triggered a broad rally in the US stock market. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week, one of its worst performances since the 2008 financial crisis.Technology stocks linked to artificial intelligence led the gains, pushing the Nasdaq Composite up 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1,117 points.Signs of a rebound had emerged even before Wall Street opened and Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement.Futures trading indicated that US stocks were poised to break a seven-session losing streak, with markets expected to open more than 2% higher.Meanwhile, European technology stocks also climbed 4.7% after Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.The decision represents a big departure of course for Nvidia's board, which had ruled out Huang's reinstatement only days earlier.Huang stepped down on November 12 following disclosures about extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for China. Beijing has denied the allegation.Explaining its decision to reinstate Huang, the board said it was satisfied with his candour and leadership capabilities. It added that, after consulting senior US government officials, it had concluded that his return posed no national security risk.“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” chair of the board Harvey C. Jones said in a statement Monday.Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.In a statement, Huang said he was “honored” to be back at the company and would take on the responsibility “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”He also expressed his gratitude to Jones, interim CEO Colette Kress, who will resume her position as CFO, and Nvidia’s executive staff for steering the company through the brief period of uncertainty.“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang’s statement continued. “Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family.I can’t wait to get back to work.”Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.
Article Summary: The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week.

Indians have always loved a good bargain, whether it is haggling over daily groceries or negotiating a trade deal with another country. After all, it is not a deal until you know you have secured better terms than the next person in line!After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact. However, the deal is yet to be signed.Earlier on Wednesday, India said it could sign the agreement only after the new tariff framework is in place and investigations under Section 301 are concluded.The India-US trade deal has seen several twists and turns since negotiations began in February 2025, from tariff threats and hopes of an agreement to a sudden courtroom setback. Now, with the deal back on the table, the latest development has raised a key question: What has changed, and why is the US suddenly offering the 'tariff king' a better deal?The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.Now, Washington's willingness to give India a comparative tariff advantage over its peers has brought the negotiations back into focus.India's importance to Washington goes well beyond trade figures. Its vast consumer market, supply of affordable medicines and potential to emerge as an alternative manufacturing base to China give the US several reasons to keep the partnership strong.Tariff competitiveness is another important part of the equation. When the first-phase BTA framework was finalised, India enjoyed a tariff advantage over ASEAN nations — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia — as well as Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh.But a lower tariff does not always mean a better deal.If India's rivals secure bigger tariff cuts, their products could become cheaper in the US market, leaving Indian exporters struggling to compete. The real advantage, therefore, lies not just in lower duties but in ensuring that India remains ahead of its competitors.So, what makes India a partner Washington cannot afford to overlook?India's importance to the US goes beyond trade, particularly when it comes to medicines. The country supplies 47% of US generic prescription drugs and 60% of hypertension medicines. Steep tariffs could hit American consumers and patients first.Rohit Kumar Singh of Eminence Strategy Consulting warns, “Disruption in supply might impact American citizens directly.”Replacing approved manufacturers, he adds, takes both investment and time.Even when the US threatened a 100% tariff on pharmaceutical imports, India remained largely shielded. Generics account for over 90% of medicines used in America and were exempted to avoid shortages and price spikes.Similarly, under the February 6 framework, the US had proposed scrapping reciprocal tariffs on Indian generics and their ingredients, with further concessions subject to a separate US investigation.The proposed purchases under the interim trade framework also give American businesses a reason to support closer trade ties with India.Under an earlier statement, India had indicated its intention to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years. These included energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal.For perspective, India's imports from all countries stood at $527.21 billion during April-October 2026-27.Singh adds that pushing India too hard could jeopardise these potential sales.As Sandeep Gupta of Executive Access sums it up, “It’s a ‘we can scratch each other’s back effectively’ deal that works for both sides.”With over 140 crore people, India is a shopper's paradise for American brands. Nearly 65% of Indians are under 35, and rising household incomes are expected to drive demand across categories, from appliances and cars to IT services. This creates opportunities for American companies selling technology, parts and financing.Geopolitics expert Jagvinder Singh Virk told TOI, “This young demographic, our expanding middle class, growing purchasing power and rapidly developing economy make India one of the most attractive markets in the world.”The US already sold India $45.4 billion worth of goods and $42.9 billion worth of services in 2025, according to USTR. Walking away from the partnership could mean losing access to an expanding market and future customers.Global companies do not just want to sell in India; they also want to manufacture here and benefit from its growth.Virk says, “India is also emerging as a trusted global manufacturing and supply-chain partner.”Despite a bumpy global economic environment, India's exports grew over 16% in the first seven months of FY 2026-27.The US increasingly sees India as a strategic economic partner rather than just another trading destination. Its willingness to offer the country a tariff advantage over competing economies also reflects India's growing bargaining power in trade negotiations.India-US relations extend beyond trade, with both countries sharing strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.One example is the Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, which focuses on cooperation in maritime security and critical technologies. In May 2026, the four countries launched an Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance project and a framework to strengthen critical-mineral supply chains.Singh cautions that any weakening of this partnership “will make it harder to implement plans to develop alternatives to concentrated supply networks.”Ritik Bhandari, team lead, Centre for Law, Policy and Governance, NFPRC Foundation says that India's growing importance to the US is driven by both economic opportunities and shared strategic interests.He further points out that India offers Washington a large consumer base, manufacturing capabilities and scope for collaboration in technology and energy. Its role in diversifying global supply chains and strengthening the US presence in the Indo-Pacific further adds to its importance.The proposed tariff advantage, he says, reflects Washington's intention to ensure India remains competitive against other trading partners.For years, China has been America's factory floor, supplying everything from electronics to industrial components. But Washington is now looking to reduce that dependence, and India is emerging as an important alternative.Gupta said, “The US wants to reduce its dependence on China-dominated manufacturing items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, minerals and manufacturing, which India can effectively offer.”US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer echoed this view in an interview with Fox News, acknowledging that “India can be a way station for that.”Losing India's trust, therefore, could prove costly for Washington on two fronts. American exporters risk losing access to Indian consumers, while US manufacturers could find themselves with fewer alternatives to Chinese suppliers.India has made it clear that a trade deal cannot come at any cost. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had earlier said negotiations had reached a stage where further give-and-take would be “very, very difficult”, describing the pact as a “hard and very vigorously negotiated agreement”.Both countries, however, maintain that they are working towards a fair and mutually beneficial deal. US embassy deputy chief of mission Jason Meeks recently described the proposed partnership as “fair, reciprocal, and mutually beneficial”, with cooperation extending beyond goods.According to Jagvinder Singh Virk, India changed the tone of negotiations with “a clear economic vision, well-defined priorities and a willingness to find practical solutions”. New Delhi, he said, had shown that it could protect its core interests while remaining flexible where both sides stood to gain.Washington, too, has reasons not to push too hard. India offers US companies a vast consumer market, a young workforce, growing manufacturing capabilities and an opportunity to diversify supply chains.Comparing the talks with negotiations involving Canada and South Korea, Virk said India's growing economic strength and strategic importance set it apart.India, meanwhile, remains firm on sensitive sectors such as agriculture and dairy. It is open to a deal, but wants one that safeguards its interests and recognises its growing economic role.India-US ties may finally be turning a corner.Chief economic adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said recent weeks had shown signs of easing tensions, adding that a trade deal in early December could mean “we may have seen the worst of the unsettled phase behind us”.One of the bigger questions is whether the agreement can help India reduce its dependence on China. Initiatives such as Make in India, the PLI scheme and Aatmanirbhar Bharat offer a starting point. However, India must build its own manufacturing capabilities rather than simply replace dependence on China with dependence on the US.The next step, therefore, is to strengthen domestic capacity. Bhandari added that manufacturing incentives could encourage Indian companies to produce more raw materials at home, while long-term US orders could help fund these facilities."The government's focus on domestic manufacturing, infrastructure development and initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides a strong foundation for this transition. Importantly, India is approaching this partnership from a position of strategic autonomy, seeking to expand international economic cooperation while strengthening its domestic capabilities.This is an opportunity to reinforce India's economic resilience and global standing," Bhandari said.At the same time, India needs to find alternative sources for critical inputs. The real opportunity is not just to become an alternative to China, but to emerge as a manufacturing and technology powerhouse in its own right.
Article Summary: After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies. The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. But the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.

Article Title: Coca-Cola bought Gold Spot from Parle Bisleri in 1993, but discontinued it in 2000 to make way for Fanta; 26 years later it is set to be re-launched with a low- or no-sugar version amid rising competi
Article Text:
Unlike colas, which account for the bulk of the Rs 60,000 crore aerated drinks market, orange-flavoured beverages represent a relatively small share of overall sales. (Image for representative purpose only)

The return of Gold Spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Coca-Cola is preparing to bring back its orange carbonated drink Gold Spot after a gap of 26 years. The move comes at a time when the competition in the beverage market intensifies and demand for sugar-free products gathers pace, people familiar with the development said.Coca-Cola’s Indian arm bought Gold Spot in 1993 from Ramesh Chauhan, the owner of Parle Bisleri, along with Thums Up and Limca. The Atlanta-headquartered beverage company discontinued Gold Spot shortly after the acquisition to make room for Fanta, its global brand.“Gold Spot is returning as a low-sugar, no-sugar drink, so it won’t cannibalise on Fanta. It is expected to be on shelves starting next week,” one of the executives aware of the developments, told ET.Meanwhile, photographs and posts circulating on social media over the weekend showed former India cricket captain MS Dhoni and his wife with cans of Gold Spot. The posts went viral, although it remains unclear whether Dhoni has been signed on as the brand’s endorser.Gold Spot, which was promoted with the tagline ‘zing thing’, was withdrawn by Coca-Cola in 2000 as the company sought to make way for Fanta.“Market share gain of legacy brands being revived after a long gap depends entirely on adequate investments in distribution, product and go-to-market,” the executive cited above told the financial daily.“Some like Thums Up, however, have always led the Indian cola market, ahead of Coca-Cola’s own global brand Coke as well as rival Pepsi, even without investments in the early years.”Unlike colas, which account for the bulk of the Rs 60,000 crore aerated drinks market, orange-flavoured beverages represent a relatively small share of overall sales.Gold Spot’s planned comeback comes at a time when consumers are increasingly turning towards healthier alternatives. The market is also facing intense competition, while New Delhi has proposed a regulatory requirement for red hexagonal labels on the front of all food and beverage packs to indicate excessive levels of sugar, salt and fat.In recent months, brands such as Reliance Consumer Products’ Campa, Lahori Zeera and Bindu Zeera, along with newer products including ITC’s Coconut Cola and Veera Foods’ Zyro, have challenged the long-standing dominance of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo in India for the first time.At the same time, sales of Coca-Cola’s mid-calorie and sugar-free beverages have risen sharply. These include zero- and no-sugar variants under its flagship Coke, Sprite and Thums Up brands, as well as Schweppes, Powerade and Rimzim. Sales of these products have doubled this year compared with last year, according to two bottling industry associates.The associates said diet and light beverages now account for more than 60% of Coca-Cola’s annual sales, up from around 30% last year.Varun Beverages, PepsiCo’s bottling associate, has also recorded a sharp increase in demand for beverages with reduced or no sugar. Sales of these products doubled to 88% of its total volumes in the July-September 2026 quarter, compared with 44% in the corresponding period a year earlier. The category also includes water and sodas.
Article Summary: Coca-Cola’s Indian arm bought Gold Spot in 1993 from Ramesh Chauhan, the owner of Parle Bisleri, along with Thums Up and Limca. Atlanta-headquartered beverage company discontinued Gold Spot shortly after the acquisition to make room for Fanta.

Article Title: India's first bullet train to begin trials on 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch in May 2027 as electrification is completed and signalling work is expected to finish by January
Article Text:
The contract covers the design, manufacture and commissioning of two train sets, each comprising eight coaches. (Design image of bullet train for representative purpose)

Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor:

When will India get its first bullet train?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

More bullet train projects

India’s first bullet train project is likely to begin trial runs in May 2027, with preparations under way to test the 50 kilometres long Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor first, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Monday.The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, India’s first bullet train project, is being developed to establish high-speed rail connectivity between the two major cities.Speaking at a media briefing, Vaishnaw said electrification work on the section was complete, while signalling-related work was scheduled to be finished by January 2027.The overhead electrification system along the elevated stretch was energised on November 20, covering both tracks. The section uses a 2x25 kV traction system, and installation work at the Bilimora traction substation has also been completed.Vaishnaw said the high-speed rail corridor would become operational in stages, rather than being opened along its entire length at one time.Under the proposed schedule, the Ahmedabad-Vapi section is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The bullet train service is targeted to extend to Thane by 2029.The first round of trials will use the B-28 train, which has been built to run at speeds of up to 280 kmph.Vaishnaw explained that operating trains at speeds exceeding 240 kmph calls for specialised engineering, as the pressure forces generated while trains are in motion must be accounted for in the design of both the rolling stock and the supporting infrastructure.He said the B-28 train had cleared a squeeze test, during which it was subjected to pressure levels twice the atmospheric pressure expected during regular operations. The test was conducted to assess the train’s ability to withstand pressure-related stresses at high speeds.The minister also expressed satisfaction with the pace of construction in Maharashtra, including work on the undersea tunnel, describing the progress on these sections as encouraging.India makes bullet train for the first timeBEML Limited has secured a Rs 866.87 crore contract from Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai, to manufacture two prototype bullet train, or high-speed train, sets designed to run at speeds exceeding 250 kmph. The trains will have a design speed of 280 kmph.The contract covers the design, manufacture and commissioning of two train sets, each comprising eight coaches.The trains will feature fully air-conditioned chair cars equipped with world-class passenger facilities, advanced onboard infotainment systems, reclining and rotatable seats, and dedicated amenities for divyangjans.To facilitate production, BEML has established a dedicated ‘Aditya’ High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru for manufacturing the bullet trains.The trains, designated as B-28 train sets, will be built using advanced, precision-driven technologies. While bullet trains operating in countries such as Japan and across Europe are engineered to withstand cold climatic conditions, the Indian versions will be designed to cope with the country’s heat and dust.The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor is one of several ambitious rail infrastructure projects planned by Indian Railways. The Union Budget for this year announced seven additional high-speed rail corridors. Developing domestic capabilities to manufacture bullet trains could help India meet the rolling stock requirements of these proposed routes more cost-effectively.The seven proposed corridors are Mumbai-Pune, with a journey time of 48 minutes; Pune-Hyderabad, at 1 hour 55 minutes; Hyderabad-Bengaluru, at 2 hours; Hyderabad-Chennai, at 2 hours 55 minutes; Chennai-Bengaluru, at 1 hour 13 minutes; Delhi-Varanasi, at 3 hours 50 minutes; and Varanasi-Siliguri via Patna, at 2 hours 55 minutes.
Article Summary: India’s first bullet train project is likely to begin trial runs in May 2027. The first round of trials will use the B-28 train, built to run at speeds of up to 280 kmph. BEML Limited has secured a Rs 866.87 crore contract from Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai, to manufacture two prototype bullet train sets.

Article Title: Year-round tax planning for salaried employees: a 12-month approach explained
Article Text:
Done steadily, tax planning stops being stressful. It turns a deadline into a routine, aligns your tax with your actual financial life.

By Archit Gupta

Start with an estimate, in April

The 12-month Tax-Planning Tracker

Choose the regime deliberately, not by habit

Align your TDS with reality

Key deduction limits FY 2026-27

Spread your deductions across the year

Review at the midpoint

Do's and don'ts for regime selection

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(The author is Founder and CEO, ClearTax)

Every person’s personal finance rests on three things. The first is protecting yourself and your family through life and health insurance. The second is your home, and the loan that usually comes with it. The third is building wealth, turning your savings into a corpus that grows over time, whether that corpus is a retirement fund decades away or simply money set aside for a year-end holiday. What ties the three together is that each has a tax side.The insurance you buy, the home loan you service, the investments you choose- every one of them can shape your tax, and deciding on them thoughtfully can leave more money in your hands. That is why tax planning works best not as a year-end scramble in March, but as a steady, year-round discipline woven into these everyday decisions. Here is how a salaried employee can approach it across twelve months.The foundation of good planning is an early estimate of your liability. At the start of the financial year, add up your expected salary, any income outside it such as interest, rent or capital gains, and the deductions you realistically expect to claim.This one exercise tells you your likely tax for the year, and it is what every later decision rests on. Without it, you are saving and investing blind, and you discover your actual position only when it is too late to change it.An estimate also reveals the size of the decision in front of you. Someone who will owe very little needs to do almost nothing; someone with a larger liability can see exactly how much planning is worth, and plan proportionately.The most consequential decision is which tax regime to use. The new regime, now the default, offers lower rates across wider slabs but withdraws most deductions. The old regime keeps higher rates but allows house rent allowance, Section 80C investments, health insurance under Section 80D, home-loan interest and more.The practical way to choose is a break-even test: the old regime is cheaper only if your total deductions cross a break-even level, and that level rises with income. Take a salaried person earning around Rs 20 lakh a year. For the old regime to beat the new, they would need roughly Rs 7 lakh of deductions, over and above the standard deduction. At exactly that break-even point, both regimes leave them with the same tax, a little over Rs 1.9 lakh.If their deductions fall short of that, the new regime is cheaper and simpler; if they comfortably exceed it, the old regime pulls ahead. For many salaried people, especially those without a home loan or large Section 80C commitments, reaching that level is difficult, which is why the new regime often works out better by default.The real error is not choosing one regime over the other; it is choosing out of habit without running both sets of numbers on your own income. This decision belongs at the start of the year, not at filing, because the regime you expect to use sets how much tax your employer deducts each month.Your employer deducts tax every month based on the regime and investments you declare, so declaring them early keeps your monthly deductions accurate and your take-home steady. The part that needs your active attention is income your employer cannot see: interest, capital gains or freelance earnings.Where your tax on that, after TDS, is likely to exceed Rs 10,000 for the year, it must be paid as advance tax in instalments across June, September, December and March. Tracking it through the year avoids a last-minute crunch and the interest that comes with missing it.The heart of year-round planning is spreading deductions over twelve months instead of bunching them into March.Under Section 80C, up to Rs 1.5 lakh is deductible. Rather than a single lump sum in March, a monthly contribution, a SIP into an equity-linked savings scheme, or regular provident fund and PPF additions spreads the cost and averages your investment price. Your EPF contribution and your children's tuition fees already count towards this limit.Health insurance, under Section 80D, allows up to Rs 25,000, rising to Rs 50,000 where you insure senior-citizen parents, a separate limit from your own family's cover. Paying premiums when the policy falls due, rather than scrambling in March, keeps both the cover and the deduction intact.The National Pension System offers an additional Rs 50,000 deduction under Section 80CCD(1B), over and above 80C. A small monthly contribution builds this painlessly. Notably, an employer's NPS contribution under Section 80CCD(2) remains available even under the new regime, one of the few benefits that survives it.If you pay rent, keep your rent receipts and your landlord's PAN, which is required where annual rent crosses Rs 1 lakh, through the year rather than reconstructing them at the end. Treated monthly, these choices ease cash flow and, more importantly, get made for sound financial reasons rather than to beat a deadline.Plans drift. A bonus, a job change, a new source of income or a shift in investments can all move your liability.A single mid-year review, around September or October, lets you correct course: adjust your declared investments, top up a shortfall, or revise your advance-tax estimate while there is still time to act.Do run both regimes on your actual numbers before deciding, and decide at the start of the year. Do declare your regime and investments to your employer early. Do keep documentation through the year. Do revisit the decision if your income changes.Don't lock money away or buy insurance purely to save tax; the deduction should follow a genuine need, not drive it. Don't leave the regime to default or habit without checking. Don't wait for March, when rushed proofs and hurried investments are exactly where costly mistakes are made. And don't overlook income outside your salary, which can quietly trigger advance tax.Done steadily, tax planning stops being stressful. It turns a deadline into a routine, aligns your tax with your actual financial life, and usually leaves more money in your hands. The best time to begin is the first month of the financial year, not the last.
Article Summary: Tax planning works best not as a year-end scramble in March, but as a steady, year-round discipline woven into these everyday decisions. The foundation of good planning is an early estimate of your liability. Spread your deductions across the year and review at the midpoint.

Article Title: From a Himalayan village to building a cybersecurity giant: Jay Chaudhry’s remarkable journey
Article Text:
Off-grid to the cloud:Jay Chaudhry’s Zscaler

Bengaluru:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Even as the cybersecurity industry witnesses a mega-deal, with CrowdStrike acquiring Zscaler in a $43 billion transaction, the story of Zscaler founder and serial tech entrepreneur Jay Chaudhry is a reminder of how extraordinary dreams can take root in the most unlikely places — even on a farm.Born into a family of small farmers in a tiny village in the foothills of the Himalayas, on the Punjab-Himachal Pradesh border, about 30 km from the Bhakra Nangal dam, Chaudhry grew up with few of the amenities that urban India took for granted. “Our village got electricity when I finished 8th grade, running water when I finished 10th grade. I sat in a car for the first time after 12th grade. And I had a flight for the first time when I went to America to do my Master’s,” he told TOI in an interview in 2020.His parents encouraged him to study because they had not had the opportunity themselves. His father had dropped out after Class 5 because the nearest middle school was too far away to walk to.Chaudhry was academically gifted, and his teachers took an interest in him. He recalls one teacher in Class 10 telling him: “You’re wasting your time in the class. Go and sit in those bushes and read. Come back, do your assignments and show me your assignments twice a day.”For pre-university (Class 11), he joined a college at the district headquarters, about 12 km away, a distance he would cover by bicycle. He went on to become a gold medallist at Himachal University. He initially considered studying engineering at Punjab Engineering College, but a teacher told him about the IITs and their system of admitting top performers from universities.“I didn’t even know about the IITs then,” Chaudhry said.He applied for electronics engineering and secured admission to IIT-BHU. Moving from a village in Himachal Pradesh to the metropolitan environment of BHU was a cultural shock, but he adapted. With many students talking about pursuing higher studies in the US, he too applied during his final year.The University of Cincinnati, Ohio, offered him a tuition scholarship. A Tata scholarship programme for students going abroad helped him fund his airline ticket.“It was just luck and it comes together sometimes,” he said modestly.Chaudhry earned a Master’s degree in computer engineering and another in industrial engineering from the University of Cincinnati, where he also met his wife, Jyoti, an MBA graduate from IIM Calcutta. He later worked at IBM and a few other companies before deciding to strike out on his own.The internet boom of the 1990s had spawned a wave of successful startups, and Chaudhry wanted to build a company in internet security. But finding funding proved difficult. One day, Jyoti confronted him: “Hey, you keep talking about it (starting a venture). Either you do something or you shut up.”Chaudhry told her that the only way to get started was to put their life savings into the venture. Jyoti brought a combination of technology and finance expertise to the table. The two decided to take the risk and jointly founded SecureIT in 1996.“It was probably the biggest and best gamble of our lives,” he says.Within two years, SecureIT was acquired by VeriSign for $70 million. The Atlanta-based venture became a success story, with 70 of its 80 employees becoming millionaires.With the proceeds from the sale, the couple went on to establish three more startups in quick succession, all of which were acquired. Chaudhry’s entrepreneurial journey included AirDefense, a wireless security pioneer acquired by Motorola; CipherTrust, which he founded in 2000 and led until its merger with Secure Computing in 2006; and CoreHarbor, a managed ecommerce solutions company acquired by USi/AT&T.By 2007, he was looking to build “something big, something special, something lasting”. Having watched software-as-a-service companies such as Salesforce and NetSuite gain traction, he became convinced that security, too, would have to move to the cloud. That conviction led to the founding of Zscaler in 2008.Zscaler went public on March 16, 2018, and has since emerged as a major player in cloud security, with customers including GE, Siemens and Shell.Chaudhry recalled meeting Jim Fowler, then CIO of GE, in 2019. “I said, Jim, thank you for making time to see me, even though we are such a small fraction of your IT budget. He smiled and said, ‘Even though you’re a small part of the budget, without Zscaler, I have no cloud strategy. I want you to come and see me every six months.’”Chaudhry and his family have a 34% stake in Zscaler. The CrowdStrike acquisition values that stake at nearly $15 billion.
Article Summary: Jay Chaudhry was born into a family of small farmers in a tiny village in the foothills of the Himalayas. His parents encouraged him to study because they had not had the opportunity themselves. He initially considered studying engineering at Punjab Engineering College, but a teacher told him about the IITs.

Article Title: Man sells property to a senior citizen for Rs 32 lakh and accepts Rs 6.75 lakh cash payment; Income Tax Department sends notice and imposes 100% penalty, but ITAT Chennai cancels it after examining ex
Article Text:
The home seller said he weighed his urgent need to sell the property against the buyer's circumstances. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT Chennai rule in favour of the property seller?

Hindustan Steel Ltd. v. State of Orissa

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Can you accept cash above a certain limit for a property sale? The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai, has directed the Income Tax Department to delete a Rs 6.75 lakh penalty imposed on a property seller who accepted an advance in cash towards the sale of his residential property.The man faced action from the Income Tax Department after he sold his residential property for Rs 32 lakh to a senior citizen.The tribunal held that the circumstances surrounding the transaction established reasonable cause under Section 273B of the Income-tax Act, 1961, providing relief from the penalty imposed under Section 271D.The issue arose when the property seller accepted Rs 6.75 lakh of the sale consideration in cash, with the balance being paid into his bank account. The payment arrangement was also recorded in the registered sale deed.However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) initiated proceedings after receiving information from the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) in Virugambakkam and examining the registered sale deed. The AO concluded that accepting the cash payment violated Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act and issued a notice.The home seller said he needed to sell his house urgently and had approached a broker to find a buyer.The broker subsequently located a senior citizen who agreed to visit Chennai to inspect the property.When the prospective buyer arrived, he was carrying Rs 6.75 lakh in cash. After viewing the house, he liked the property and made an offer to purchase it immediately. To finalise the deal, he proposed paying Rs 6.75 lakh as an advance in cash.The buyer told the home seller that he did not want to take the money all the way back, nor did he wish to postpone the transaction until he could arrange payment through banking channels.The home seller said he weighed his urgent need to sell the property against the buyer's circumstances. He also believed that refusing the cash would leave the senior citizen with the risk of carrying Rs 6.75 lakh back. He therefore accepted the amount in good faith.He maintained that he had disclosed the cash payment in the sale deed and reported the entire property transaction in his income tax return (ITR), believing that these disclosures would meet the requirements of the Income Tax Act.Of the total sale price of Rs 32 lakh, Rs 6.75 lakh was received in cash as an advance, while the remaining consideration was paid into his bank account. The full sale amount was documented in the sale deed.The proceedings culminated in a penalty of Rs 6.75 lakh being imposed on the home seller for accepting cash in connection with the property sale.He challenged the penalty and secured a favourable ruling from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai.One of the key considerations was that the man had not attempted to hide the cash component of the property sale. He had disclosed the payment in the registered sale deed, reported the transaction in his income tax return (ITR), deposited the money in his bank account and paid capital gains tax after disclosing the transaction.The tribunal examined whether the man qualified for relief under Section 273B of the Income Tax Act, which provides protection from penalties when a taxpayer can demonstrate reasonable cause for failing to comply with the law.The ITAT considered the seller’s explanation alongside the circumstances surrounding the transaction. It noted that the CIT(A) had not disputed the genuineness of the sale, the deposit of the advance into the seller’s bank account, the receipt of the balance consideration through banking channels or the recording of the full consideration in the registered sale deed.The tribunal cautioned that these circumstances did not independently establish reasonable cause. However, it considered them material when assessing the seller’s explanation collectively. It observed: “Although these circumstances do not, individually, establish reasonable cause, they are material factors supporting the assessee's explanation regarding the bona fide circumstances in which the cash advance was accepted. ”The bench found that the CIT(A) had not adequately assessed the combined effect of these circumstances while deciding whether the seller qualified for relief under Section 273B. It held: “Consequently, the conclusion reached by the ld.CIT(A) that the assessee had failed to establish reasonable cause cannot be sustained on the facts and circumstances of the present case.”The tribunal also considered earlier decisions of the Chennai and Visakhapatnam benches involving cash received towards property sales. Its discussion included the Supreme Court’s decision in, which formed part of the legal background concerning the imposition of penalties. The decisive finding in this case, however, was that the seller had established reasonable cause under Section 273B when the circumstances were considered together.The ITAT concluded: “The contravention of section 269SS of the Act, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, is therefore covered by the statutory protection provided u/s.273B of the Act.”Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that ITAT held that Section 269SS did not apply to this case. It also clarified that a breach of Section 269SS does not, by itself, automatically establish a violation of Section 271D.Surana said the assessee’s actions lent credibility to his explanation that he had accepted the cash because he genuinely believed the senior citizen buyer’s account of his circumstances. They also supported his contention that he had no intention of suppressing or concealing the transaction.Surana said the ruling highlights how Section 273B can offer protection from penalties when a taxpayer provides a genuine and reasonable explanation for accepting cash in a property transaction and transparently records the payment in the ITR, sale deed and other relevant documents.
Article Summary: The man faced action from the Income Tax Department after he sold his residential property for Rs 32 lakh to a senior citizen. He accepted Rs 6.75 lakh of the sale consideration in cash, with the balance being paid into his bank account. The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) concluded that accepting the cash payment violated Section 269SS of the Income tax Act.

Article Title: DG: RBI using alternate data sources for forecasts
Article Text: MUMBAI: RBI is increasingly using alternative data sources, including FASTag transactions, satellite imagery and digital payment metrics, to forecast economic activity and inform policy decisions, supplementing official data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI).The alternative indicators provide early signals of economic trends before conventional data become available. "For forward-looking policy, we complement hard data, as they become available, with alternative data that are available in near real time and can carry early information about what may be coming," said Poonam Gupta, deputy governor, RBI.She was speaking at a MoSPI-organised data users conference on the new series of gross domestic product (GDP), consumer price index (CPI) and index of industrial production (IIP). Gupta identified FASTag transactions as an indicator of freight movement, alongside GST collections, e-way bills and digital payment metrics. RBI also uses satellite imagery, together with ground-level environmental data, to assess weather shocks and agricultural output.
Article Summary: RBI is increasingly using alternative data sources to forecast economic activity and inform policy decisions. Alternative indicators provide early signals of economic trends before conventional data become available. FASTag transactions, GST collections, e-way bills and digital payment metrics are used.

Article Title: SC to appoint sole arbitrator for Kalyani family dispute
Article Text: NEW DELHI: With former SC judge L N Rao's mediation failing to resolve the Kalyani group family dispute estimated at Rs 1 lakh crore, Supreme Court on Monday said it will appoint a sole arbitrator with the consent of parties to comprehensively decide all disputes, both corporate management and family wealth.The dispute, primarily between Bharat Forge chairperson Baba Kalyani, his sister Sugandha Hiremath and his brother Gaurishankar Kalyani, was referred to Justice Rao for mediation by the SC in July. The Bombay HC had felt that there was no realistic chance of success in resolving the dispute through mediation.When Gaurishankar's counsel N K Kaul said he has suggested a comprehensive settlement proposal which would resolve all pending disputes, Baba's counsel A M Singhvi said he would seek instruction from his client on the proposal as well as the court's suggestion for arbitration. SC posted the matter for further hearing after two weeks.
Article Summary: Kalyani group family dispute estimated at Rs 1 lakh crore. Dispute primarily between Bharat Forge chairperson Baba Kalyani and his sister Sugandha Hiremath. Former SC judge L N Rao's mediation failed to resolve the dispute.

Article Title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO bid 1.5 times
Article Text: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields closed on Monday with the issue subscribed 1.5 times. Institutional investors took the lead in bidding.Institutional investors bid for 55.7 crore shares against nearly 11.3 crore shares on offer, resulting in almost five times oversubscription for this portion, according to NSE website data. The portion reserved for non-institutional investors (also called the high net worth investors or HNIs) was subscribed only 66% as the total bids were for nearly 5.6 crore shares compared to 8.4 crore shares on offer. The part reserved for retail investors too was undersubscribed with less than half the 19.7 crore shares on offer being bid for. The shareholders' portion was subscribed 56% while the employees' portion was subscribed 22%. TNN

Article Title: Brookfield to buy PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion
Article Text:
Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion, with the deal expected to close in Q1 2027.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Global investment firm Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity for $1.7 billion.The transaction, which is subject to regulatory and govt approvals, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Brookfield will fund the acquisition through its Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation.PGP Glass manufactures premium glass packaging for cosmetics, perfumes, pharmaceuticals and specialty food and beverages. The company operates three manufacturing facilities across India and Sri Lanka and supplies packaging to global brands in more than 70 countries.The company has 13 furnaces and a production capacity of more than 1,800 tonnes per day. Overseas markets account for more than 70% of its sales. Brookfield plans to expand PGP Glass's presence in international markets, deepen relationships with existing customers and invest in additional manufacturing capacity. It also intends to introduce artificial intelligence across the company's operations, including production planning, manufacturing efficiency and quality control.Aditya Joshi, managing partner and head of private equity for Brookfield in Asia Pacific and the Middle East, said, "As demand for high-quality packaging continues to increase worldwide, Brookfield brings the scale and operating expertise to accelerate PGP's growth through an AI-led transformation program."The investment comes as glass packaging manufacturers in Europe and North America face rising costs and rationalise capacity. Brookfield sees an opportunity for manufacturers such as PGP, which have lower production costs, to gain market share in premium packaging.Blackstone said its investment in PGP had helped the company expand manufacturing capacity, improve operations and strengthen its sustainability initiatives.Amit Dalmia, senior managing director and head of the Blackstone Operating Team in Asia, said the company's management had delivered strong operating performance and outpaced its peers during Blackstone's ownership. PGP Glass CEO Vijay Shah said Brookfield's international presence and operational experience would support the company's next phase of growth. He also credited Blackstone's partnership with helping PGP expand capacity and strengthen its operations.
Article Summary: Global investment firm Brookfield has agreed to acquire specialty glass packaging manufacturer PGP Glass. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. PGP manufactures premium glass packaging for cosmetics, perfumes, pharmaceuticals and specialty food and beverages.

Article Title: Sebi warns against IPO grey market premium
Article Text:
Sebi warned all its regulated entities not to promote or publish GMPs of IPO-bound companies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Sebi on Monday warned investors about grey market premiums (GMPs) in IPOs, the pre-listing premium figures that are available on unofficial sites. The markets regulator said it has come to its notice that trades based on GMPs are being carried out through platforms that are "unofficial, unverified, and unregulated," even before they are listed on the bourses. "These transactions are executed outside the exchange framework, are not subject to regulatory oversight, carry no settlement guarantee or investor protection, and follow no formal price-discovery process."A Sebi release said that while investing in the securities market, investors are advised not to treat GMP as an indicator of listing price or expected returns. It also said that investors should refrain from engaging in any GMP-linked transactions, as they fall entirely outside the regulatory framework.It also asked all investors to transact in IPOs exclusively through Sebi-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms.Sebi warned all its regulated entities not to promote or publish GMPs of IPO-bound companies. It also advised all publications against writing about GMPs or such pre-listing premium figures in the interests of investors and "contrary to the core principles of transparency and accountability in the securities market."
Article Summary: Sebi warned investors about grey market premiums (GMPs) in IPOs. GMPs are pre- listing premium figures that are available on unofficial sites. Sebi warned all its regulated entities not to promote or publish GMPs of IPO-bound companies.

NEW DELHI: Tata Steel on Monday said it has executed an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 15,510 crore and plans to take over another 26% in the pipes and tubes maker through an open offer of Rs 16,756 crore, a move that will increase the Tata group firm's downstream production capabilities three times.The deal will enable Tata Steel to expand steel tubes and colour-coated products output to 7.5 million tonnes per annum, from 2.5 MTPA at present.
